input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The duplicate-numbered § 12.4 (p0046) binds the Customer to a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months, covering any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. That is walk-away territory under the rule (post-term restriction longer than 12 months and effectively undefined scope) and fails the fallback on every material term: scope, duration and carve-outs. It also directly contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. The smallest fix that reaches the preferred position is deletion of p0046, leaving § 12.3 to govern; a narrowed term-only restriction on a single named product is offered as a fallback in the comment. The separate no-hire covenant at p0045 is left for the applicable no-hire rule.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the products or services we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted the second § 12.4 competitive-activity ban, which also directly contradicts § 12.3. If Cobalt needs protection, we could consider a narrow term-only restriction on a single named competing product, capped at 12 months with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month, all-territory non-compete imposed on Customer.
